_why: This file is where an inferred answer goes so that it is answered ONCE instead of once per application.
draft_form_spec.py loads it and tries these rules BEFORE its built-in table, because a rule here was written by
hand for a wording that recurred, while the built-in table is a heuristic over general English.
EVERY RULE MUST CARRY A NOTE NAMING WHERE ITS ANSWER COMES FROM. A rule that cites nothing cannot be told apart
from a guess by the next reader, and because it matches, the question will never be listed in needs_review again -
so nobody will look at it a second time either.
A rule that only restates a general wording belongs in draft_form_spec.py's matchers instead. Put a rule here when
the wording is tenant-specific or boilerplate-specific, like a form that asks about the company by name.
`kind` is optional and narrows the rule to one control type (text | select | check); leaving it out lets the rule
answer the question on any control.

rules.note: EXAMPLE RULE - canonical: no employer in data/application_profile.json is this tenant. Before trusting it, check the tracker: 'have you applied to us before' is a different question with a different answer. Replace this rule's note with the source you actually relied on.

rules.questionRe: country/region do you have citizenship|which country.*citizenship|citizenship.*country
rules.note: EXAMPLE RULE - canonical: candidate.citizenship in data/candidate_profile.json. The value must be the form's OWN option text for that country, not a free-text spelling, because the filler selects an option by its text. Citizenship is not immigration status and neither is work authorisation; never answer one from the other.

rules.questionRe: notice period|how much notice|when (can|could) you start
rules.answer: Example: four weeks from the date of an offer
rules.note: EXAMPLE RULE - user rule: the availability answer you decided on, recorded here with its date and your own words. A notice period is a statement about your current employer's contract, so it must never be guessed from a job description.
